statement: Nine dots are arranged in a square array of 3 rows of 3, equally spaced. How many triangles have all three of their corners at these dots?

choices.misconception: I removed the sets of three dots that lie along a row or a column but forgot the two diagonals.
I removed only the four lines through the middle dot: the middle row, the middle column and the two diagonals.
I counted every way to choose three of the nine dots, forgetting that three dots in a straight line make no triangle.
I counted 9 × 8 × 7 ordered choices of corners, so each triangle was counted once for every order of its corners.

hints: Any three dots make a triangle unless they lie on one straight line.
Count all the ways to choose three of the nine dots, then subtract the choices where the three dots are in a straight line. Find every straight line that passes through three dots.
There are 84 ways to choose three dots. Three dots lie in a line along each of the 3 rows, the 3 columns and the 2 diagonals.

solutions.reliable: Three dots can be chosen in 9 × 8 × 7 / (3 × 2 × 1) = 84 ways. A choice fails to make a triangle exactly when the three dots are in a straight line. In a 3 by 3 array the only lines through three dots are the 3 rows, the 3 columns and the 2 diagonals, which is 8 lines, each giving one bad choice. So there are 84 - 8 = 76 triangles. The transferable idea: when most choices work, count everything and subtract the few that fail.
solutions.elegant: Sort by whether the middle dot is used. Without it, any 3 of the 8 outer dots work except the 4 sides of the square: 56 - 4 = 52. With it, any 2 of the 8 outer dots work except the 4 opposite pairs that line up through the middle: 28 - 4 = 24. Total 52 + 24 = 76.

whyOnTest: Counting hidden shapes is easiest with a complement: count every choice of corners and remove the degenerate ones, and the traps miss some of the straight lines.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
